payload:019d451d-04d1-7d63-a2b6-bebfb2297fcf|019d451d-06ac-7511-8ac3-f27d5cb9303a|## Files
- [/Users/bretpadres/Documents/projects/pong/main.js](main.js) — Monolithic single-file implementation containing bootstrap, state, loop, physics, rendering, input, audio, and HUD.

## Relationships
- `state` is the shared mutable backbone used by every subsystem: setup/reset, input handling, update systems, rendering, and HUD sync all read/write this object.
- Rendering reads from `state` (arena geometry, entities, timers, effects flags, score/lives/message) and does not mutate core gameplay state.
- Input (`attachEvents`) writes into `state.keyboard`, `state.running`, `state.gameOver`, `state.level`, and triggers lifecycle actions (`startGame`, `launchBall`, `resetRun`).
- Physics/collision (`updateBalls`, `updateHazards`, `updatePickups`, `updateBricks`) updates entity arrays and gameplay counters, and calls effect/audio helpers.
- Power-up/hazard event handlers (`applyPickup`, `unleashCoreVolley`, `explodeAround`, `loseLife`, `destroyBrick`) bridge collision outcomes into score, progression, timers, and next-wave logic.
- `frame` drives the loop (`update` + `drawArena`) and is the only animation driver via `requestAnimationFrame`.
- `hud` DOM bindings + `syncHud` + message/banner updates provide UI projection of the `state` model.

## Answer
### Major state buckets in `state`
- [ ] Game session state: `running`, `gameOver`, `score`, `lives`, `level`, `combo`, `comboTimer`, `overdrive`, `overdriveTimer`.
- [ ] Core timing/FX controls: `pendingWaveTimer`, `shake`, `flash`, `timeScale`, `slowTimer`, `hitStopTimer`, `message`, `messageTimer`, `powerupBanner`.
- [ ] Input/pointer state: `keyboard.left`, `keyboard.right`, `pointerX`.
- [ ] Player state: `paddle` object (`x,y,width,height,speed,baseWidth,glow,shieldTimer,multiballTimer,plasmaTimer`).
- [ ] Spatial collections: `balls`, `bricks`, `pickups`, `hazards`, `particles`, `floatingTexts`, `stars`, `rowOffsets`, `rowVelocities`.
- [ ] Engine/static settings: canvas dimensions, arena bounds, audio init (`audioReady`), audio context handle (`synth` external object).

### Game loop phases
- Frame acquisition: `frame(ts)` computes `rawDt`, enforces max dt cap, handles `hitStopTimer`.
- Update phase order inside `update(dt)`:
  1. `updatePaddle`
  2. `updateBricks`
  3. Conditional running update branch (`updateBalls`, `updateHazards`, `updatePickups`)
  4. `updateFx` (effects, timers, cleanup, HUD sync, finale trigger)
- Render phase: `drawArena` orchestrates background, entities, particles/text/banners, screen shake/flash overlays.

### Input handling
- Keyboard:
  - A/Left and D/Right for paddle movement flags.
  - Space to start game when overlay active/game over, or launch a stuck ball.
  - Escape resets and shows start overlay.
  - Ctrl+Shift+Digit0-9 jumps to level for quick entry.
- Pointer/click:
  - Canvas pointerdown launches ball when overlay not visible.
  - Start button click calls `startGame`.

### Rendering
- Draw composition is split into named draw functions:
  - `drawBackground`, `drawBricks`, `drawPaddle`, `drawBalls`, `drawPickups`, `drawHazards`, `drawParticles`, `drawTexts`, `drawPowerupBanner`.
- Shared canvas helpers: `roundRect`, `hexToRgba`.
- HUD rendering is DOM-bound via `syncHud` and message/banner DOM updates.
- Draw phase is separate from update but reads the same `state`, making it a view layer over mutable simulation state.

### Physics/collision
- Ball physics: `updateBalls` (integration, trail, wall/top boundaries, paddle reflection, brick overlap resolution, life offscreen).
- Paddle collision: `bounceBallFromPaddle` with controlled angle and speed scaling.
- Brick collision response: damage handling in `updateBalls`, collision side resolution, score triggers, brick destruction and special effects.
- Hazard collision: `updateHazards` checks paddle overlap and life handling.
- Pickup collision: `updatePickups` checks paddle overlap and invokes `applyPickup`.
- Utility clamp/reduce edge behavior: `clampBallAngle`, `loseLife` for terminal off-ball state.

### AI / opponent logic
- There is no dedicated AI or opponent controller object.
- “Opposition” behavior is data-driven/system-driven:
  - brick movement patterns in `updateBricks` (`drift`, `sentinel`, `sweep`) based on wave level.
  - hazard spawning from alive brick types in `updateHazards`.
- This behaves like deterministic/procedural adversary systems rather than player-vs-AI logic.

### Audio
- `Synth` class encapsulates all sound creation and playback:
  - oscillator-based `beep`, filtered noise `noise`, and semantic wrappers (`impact`, `brick`, `pickup`, `loss`, `launch`, `overdrive`, `hazard`).
- `synth.ensure()` on user-initiated interaction; gameplay calls trigger feedback sounds at key events.

### UI/HUD binding
- One-time DOM capture:
  - canvas/context + HUD elements (`score`, `lives`, `level`, `overdriveFill`, `message`, `combo`, overlay + start button).
- HUD updates are centralized in `syncHud`.
- Overlay lifecycle:
  - `startGame`, `loseLife`, `jumpToLevel`, reset/level transition mutate overlay title/body/button visibility/content.

### Constants / configuration
- Static constants: `TAU`, `GAME_W`, `GAME_H`, `brickTypes` (HP/score/color), HUD defaults (`defaultOverlayTitle/defaultOverlayBody`), and many inlined literals for movement/speeds/spawn timings/positions.
- This suggests a clear candidate to extract a config module (e.g., gameplay tuning constants + visual/audio tuning constants).

### Likely refactor boundaries
- `constants.js` (dimensions, brick profiles, tuning constants, timing/speed tables, input keys).
- `state.js` (initial state factory + reset helpers; avoid global shared mutation leakage).
- `systems/input.js` (keyboard/pointer overlay/game commands).
- `systems/loop.js` (`frame` + `update` orchestration, pause/hit-stop handling).
- `systems/physics.js` (`updatePaddle`, `updateBalls`, `updateBricks`, collision helpers).
- `systems/spawnAndProgression.js` (level generation, pickups/hazards lifecycle, score/life/overdrive progression).
- `systems/render.js` (draw functions + effects rendering order).
- `systems/audio.js` (`Synth` + event mapping).
- `ui/hud.js` (DOM bindings, sync/update messages, overlay management).
- `main.js` becomes composition/bootstrap only: import/init, module wiring, and `requestAnimationFrame` start.

## Next steps
- Ready to proceed with a practical migration plan into modules with zero behavior change.
- 1) Create a state + config first, 2) extract loop and systems incrementally behind a shared context object, 3) move rendering and UI to separate modules, 4) leave main.js as composition root.

payload:019d451b-824b-75e3-832f-f05f969651bd|019d451c-f5a9-7fb2-9826-4a52f4d7cbf1|Here’s the project map, optimized for architecture.

## High-level shape
This is a **single-page static browser game** with a **single-file runtime**:

- `index.html` — page shell and DOM scaffold
- `main.js` — the entire game runtime
- `styles.css` — all visual styling
- `README.md` — usage/run instructions

There’s **no build system** or package tooling in the repo; it appears to run as a plain static site.

## Runtime flow
The app starts like this:

1. `index.html` loads `styles.css`
2. `index.html` imports `main.js`
3. `main.js` initializes DOM bindings, canvas, audio, and game state
4. A `requestAnimationFrame` loop drives:
   - update
   - physics/collision
   - effects/timers
   - rendering
   - HUD sync

## Main subsystems in `main.js`

### 1) Shared game state
A single mutable `state` object is the backbone of the app.

It holds:
- session flags: `running`, `gameOver`, `score`, `lives`, `level`
- timers/effects: combo, slow/hit-stop, shake/flash, message banners
- input state: keyboard flags, pointer position
- player state: paddle properties
- world entities: balls, bricks, pickups, hazards, particles, floating text, stars
- progression data: row offsets, velocities, wave effects

### 2) Input handling
Input writes directly into shared state and can trigger lifecycle actions.

Likely responsibilities:
- keyboard left/right movement
- space to start or launch
- escape to reset
- pointer/click to launch
- debug level jump shortcuts

### 3) Game loop / orchestration
A central loop coordinates all simulation work.

Typical phase order:
1. paddle update
2. brick update
3. active gameplay updates:
   - balls
   - hazards
   - pickups
4. effects/timers cleanup
5. render

### 4) Physics and collision
This is the most gameplay-heavy part.

It handles:
- ball motion and wall/paddle collisions
- brick overlap detection and damage
- hazard/pickup collisions
- score/life changes
- loss/reset transitions

### 5) Progression and spawn logic
The “enemy” side of the game is procedural, not AI-driven.

It manages:
- brick patterns and movement
- hazard spawning
- pickup application
- combo / overdrive / wave pacing

### 6) Rendering
Rendering reads from `state` but should not mutate core gameplay state.

Draw stages likely include:
- background
- bricks
- paddle
- balls
- pickups
- hazards
- particles
- floating text
- banners / overlays

### 7) Audio
A `Synth` helper encapsulates sound generation.

It appears to provide event sounds for:
- hits
- brick destruction
- pickups
- launches
- losses
- overdrive / hazard events

### 8) UI / HUD binding
DOM elements outside the canvas are synced from state.

Likely responsibilities:
- score/lives/level display
- overlay message and button visibility
- progress bars / meters
- start/reset messaging

## Best refactor boundaries
If you later split this file, the clean boundaries are:

- `state` / reset helpers
- `input`
- `loop`
- `physics`
- `progression/spawn`
- `render`
- `audio`
- `ui/hud`
- `main.js` as a composition root only

## Practical summary
If I had to describe the codebase in one line:

> It’s a **monolithic canvas game engine** with a **single shared state object**, a **frame loop**, and separate concerns for input, simulation, rendering, audio, and HUD updates — all currently housed in `main.js`.

If you want, I can turn this into a **refactor roadmap** next, broken into safe incremental steps.
